fault-lines.look: With the strata source (random-brightness layers of a folded depth coordinate) the sheet reads as a geological cross-section: long straight fault traces, each slab shifted, and because the position is updated family by family the traces of earlier families are visibly offset where later families cross them, so true cross-cutting relationships appear. Density 0.6 (only 60 percent of slabs slip) looks more geological than every slab slipping; Zone 0.15 to 0.35 turns the scarps into drag folds that read as folded strata. Relief with Throw 0.15 on a gentle FBm is fault-block terrain with straight scarps and tilted blocks; with Throw 0 the lateral slip alone only shows where the source has a strong gradient. On isotropic 3-octave FBm the faults are barely visible (confirmed, needs structure), on Worley F1 they show as cut cells. The 3D form (planes with dip, dip-slip vectors) on sine strata gives an isosurface of stacked slabs offset along tilted planes. Wide view at window 40 shows the first family's parallel near-vertical traces at regular spacing even with boundary jitter 0.6 and pre-warp 0.6; it is faint but a per-family lattice is still there.
fault-lines.dims: 2D measured. 3D measured (Eval3: plane normals tilted by dip, slip vector blends strike and dip directions; vol rendered, sheet XZ slice shows planar cuts). 4D not attempted; the scheme is a per-family table of normal and slip vectors so it extends, but the 4D slip vector choice is arbitrary.
fault-lines.range: clamped source: over 8 seeds/offsets -0.993..0.999, mean -0.019; far coords 4e4 fine, no NaN
fault-lines.artifacts: Per-family lattice spacing faintly visible in wide views; Density and jitter reduce it but do not remove it. Slip above about half the spacing destroys slab identity.
fault-lines.node_shape: Domain modifier. Fault Count (int), Spacing (float), Slip (hybrid, fraction of spacing), Density (float 0..1), Zone Width (float, 0 = hard scarps, >0 = C1 drag folds, c0ratio 4.34 at 0.15), Boundary Jitter, Direction Seed, Throw (float added to the output per slip, for fault-block height fields), Dip (3D), Dip Slip fraction (3D), Source.
fault-lines.port_notes: Hash of (slab index, family) with the seed; per-family spacing scaled by 1 + 0.31 l and golden-angle directions. Boundary jitter needs offsets of slab i and i+1 (two hashes), Zone needs the neighbour slips (two more). Displacement bounded by Slip x Spacing per family regardless of coordinates. Throw should be its own output mode or a float; it is what makes scarps appear on a smooth height source. Document that the node needs a structured source (strata, stripes, cellular) to show.

critic.notes: True cross-cutting offsets are real and hold on seeds 1337, 7, 42, 90210, 424242. It does need structure: on FBm it leaves thin straight hairlines, on Worley cut cells. The strata source is not special: CellularValue through DomainAxisScale with a Perlin DomainOffset fold gives the same layers from stock nodes. The claim that warps and graphs cannot make slip discontinuities is false. A stock chain per family of DomainRotate, DomainOffset, Multiply, Terrace(Step Count=1), DomainAxisScale, Value reproduces the look in kind. At these settings it is busier than the node because every slipped slab gets full slip; I did not tune it further. Slabs come from level crossings of 1D Value, so spacing is irregular. Measured AVX2 ns 2D/3D/4D for 6 families over Perlin: 9.36/14.62/18.34 against plain Perlin 0.91/2.13/4.16, about 1.4 ns per family in 2D, so the node's speed gain is modest and that graph is an upper bound. A node still earns its place on use, not on look or speed: 6 families is about 36 nodes with no shared Slip control, Terrace gives only slip -1, 0, +1, stock tips via a 2D Perlin gate curl the layers instead of ending the trace (graph tips panel), 3D dip needs extra inverse rotations (stock alternating Pitch test comes out as tilted chunks), and stock DomainRotate has no 4D form, so the graph in GenTileable2D renders plain stripes with no faults. Zone is not drag: at .15 and .35 the trace vanishes and the layers just fold. Throw adds height steps but no per block tilt in the code, and the image reads as rugged hills with thin scarps, not tilted blocks. I could not see the claimed per family lattice; the wider weakness is only 6 orientations. Scalar measured, proto param lookups included: plain 10.7-11.3x, tips 13.4x, zone and tips 17.3x perlin2. Node cost itself is ESTIMATE, no real node built. 4D not tested, and straight traces will not stay straight through the torus map (reasoning, not rendered). Far coords and range fine, c0ratio 1.00 by design. Small flaw with zone plus tips: rare tiny folded chips, about 10 px in one 256 px thumb.
critic.improved: Two new parameters, both clearly better. tip: slip fades along strike by hashed 1D noise, so traces end instead of crossing the whole map; scarps in relief die out naturally. zres: fraction of slip kept as a hard jump inside a Zone, so layers bend and then break (normal drag) where the idea's Zone erased the fault. sheet, thumb, relief and vol overwritten. Previous source kept as t_fault_lines.prev.cpp.

tournament.notes: Keeper, but unique is only 5 because I built it. A stock chain of 36 nodes gives the cross-cut look in kind at 9.36/14.62/18.34 ns AVX2 over Perlin, about 1.4 ns per family in 2D, which is an upper bound on node cost, so the speed gain is modest. The case for a node is usability and reach: one Slip control, graded slip, ends and drag, clean 3D dip (the stock alternating Pitch test comes out as tilted chunks), and a 4D form the graph cannot have because DomainRotate has none, so the graph renders plain stripes when tiled. Reads as faulted strata on seeds 1337, 7, 42, 90210 and 424242. Needs a structured source; on FBm it only leaves hairlines. Only 6 orientations is the weakness I can see; I could not see the claimed per family lattice. Scalar measured, proto param lookups included: plain 10.7-11.3x, tips 13.4x, zone and tips 17.3x perlin2. Small flaw: rare folded chips with zone and tips, about 10 px in one thumb. 4D not tested, and straight traces will not stay straight through the torus map (reasoning, not rendered).
tournament.est_avx2_ns: ESTIMATE: per family one dot, floor, 2-3 hashes, a Select, about 1-1.5 ns; 6 families ~8 ns plus the source, flat across dimensions. Scalar measured 10.8x perlin2 this pass (8.2x earlier run, same build); earlier A/B of 4 families + FBm3 vs 0 families gave ~21 ns scalar per family, so take 20-35 ns scalar per family including harness overhead.

artist-terrain.note: Thumb is a geological cross-section with real cross-cutting; drag-tips discovery is the best image. Stock 36-node chain exists at ~9 ns, so the win is usability, 3D dip and 4D.

artist-material.note: Offset strata read as a geology cross section right away. Exactly what cliff materials lack.

voxel-engineer.note: Vol is the most geological 3D image here: displaced beds with clean dip. Est 8 ns + source and flat with dimension, 4D possible where the stock graph is not.

maintainer.note: Cross-cut geological section reads well with the strata source; a 36-node stock chain gives it in kind at 9-18 ns measured. Range -0.58..0.65, c0 1.03 by design. Marginal.

graphics-researcher.note: Cross-cutting offsets are a known layered-offset trick (a 36-node stock chain does it), but finite faults with drag and tips is the most geological image in the family.

creative.note: A geology diagram come to life, and the offset layered volume is lovely.

master.one_liner: Sequential families of long straight fault planes, each slab slipped by a hash, so later faults cross-cut and offset earlier ones like real geology.
master.look: Tectonic block faults with offset strata, shifted glass, broken marble and terrain with long linear scarps; with Zone it gives big sheared drag folds. Prototype with strata source reads as a geological cross-section. Prototyped: mode=9.
master.algorithm: For l in 0..Faults-1: n = dir(l) (golden-angle table), t = perpendicular to n (3D: strike or dip vector in plane). d = dot(p,n)*s_l + o_l. i = floor(d). slip = rnd11(hash(i,l)). Zone option, f = d-i: slip = s_i + (s_(i+1)-s_i)*.5*smoothstep(1-z,1,f) + (s_(i-1)-s_i)*.5*smoothstep(z,0,f). p += t*slip*Slip/s_l. Output S(p). Because p is updated in the loop, later faults displace earlier ones, giving true cross-cutting relationships. z=0: hard scarps. z>0: drag folds in shear zones, C1.
master.why_new: Voronoi-based cells have no long straight lines across the map, and no cross-cutting offsets. Warps cannot produce slip discontinuities with undisturbed blocks between them. Hard thing made easy for geology and strata.
master.simd_plan: Each family: dot, floor, 1 hash (3 with Zone), about 0.5-1 ns (estimate). 4 faults about 3 ns. Dimension agnostic through a table of n, t per dimension. Bounded displacement regardless of far coords.
master.continuity: z=0: discontinuous on purpose (c0ratio 1.02). z>0: C1 (5.07 at z=.15, steep, no jump).
master.params: Fault Count (int), Spacing (hybrid per node), Slip (hybrid), Zone Width, Direction Seed, Source.
master.risks: Fault spacing has lattice regularity per family: use jittered per-family scale (prototype uses 1 + l*.31) and pre-warp. Isotropic sources show faults only weakly; needs strata or high-gradient sources. Tilted 3D variants need checking. Slip should be well below spacing to preserve slab identity.
master.cost_note: Each family: dot, floor, 1 hash (3 with Zone), about 0.5-1 ns (estimate). 4 faults about 3 ns.

burgers-steepen.look: Perlin at t=1.5: smooth windward ramps ending in razor cliffs, an asymmetric sawtooth skyline in relief; the one-sided profile is real and nothing on the existing sheet has it. With the idea's 5-eval bisection the field has small closed islands (pinholes) where a different root is picked: counted 12 islands / 28 px in a 256x256 thumb at t=1.5, 33 / 287 px at t=3, 73 / 177 px on 5-octave FBm; in relief they are isolated pillars. The entropy root (K-tap trapezoid Hopf-Lax scan + bisection) removes them: K21+N4 gives 2 px at t=1.5 and at t=3 turns the hole-ridden picture into clean merged N-wave sawtooth; K13+N4 is 43 px (almost clean), K9 171 px, K7 313 px (no better than bisection). High-octave FBm (5 oct) at t=1.5 is torn shingles with many tiny shocks in every mode; steepening only the first octave and adding the fine octaves raw gives a shocked coarse shape with intact detail (wind-sculpted rock), which is a graph the user can build from the node. Cole-Hopf with the source treated as the potential (idea cole-hopf-dunes) gives blobby derivative-like cells, not dunes, at K=7; a viscous Cole-Hopf with the true integrated potential shows tap banding ripples at K=9..15. Rejected both.
burgers-steepen.dims: 2D measured. 3D measured (Eval3 with perlin3 and a 3D direction; check: range -0.58..0.65, dz continuity max 0.36 = shock jumps). 4D not measured; the solver is a 1D line search so it is dimension agnostic by construction.
burgers-steepen.range: mode 5 over 8 seeds/offsets: -0.855..0.862, mean 0.002; stays inside the source range by construction (root of S - v)
burgers-steepen.artifacts: Pinholes (islands of the other root) in bisection mode, scaling with t and octaves; absent at K21 and small at K13 in entropy mode. Residual slivers at t=3 even with K21 (163 px, a few small dark chips). Mean-of-taps variants show banding at tap spacing.
burgers-steepen.node_shape: Modifier with GeneratorSource Source; Time (hybrid, 0 = passthrough); Direction: Angle in 2D, X/Y/Z/W vector members otherwise; Root enum {Fast = bisection with Iterations, Entropy = Taps coarse scan + Iterations}; Iterations int (4..6); Taps int (9..13); Bound float (source bracket, 1.2).
burgers-steepen.port_notes: All lanes run fixed N (and K) iterations with Select on the sign of f = S - v; the final false-position step costs no eval. Entropy mode: trapezoid-accumulate Phi along the line while scanning, keep running min E and its index via masks, bracket between neighbouring taps. Breaking time from source max slope: 0.37 for 1-octave Perlin, 0.32 for 3, 0.23 for 5 octaves; below it the field is C1 and unique, above it root choice matters. Document that Time should be applied to coarse octaves with fine detail added after. GenTileable2D: a fixed 4D direction projects to a varying direction across the image, result still tiles. Re-measured on resume: entropy 21.5x, bisection 10.4x perlin2 (earlier run 21.0x / 9.9x).

critic.notes: One-sided fronts are real, but 'no graph can do it' is only partly true. 1 to 3 nested self DomainOffset gives blobs and rings, no cliff. A stock Add(Multiply(Modulus(Add(Gradient, Multiply(Perlin, .9)), 1.5), .5), Multiply(Perlin, .6)) does give one-sided ramps and cliffs, convincing in relief, at a measured 4.59/7.75/12.60 ns AVX2, about a third of the node estimate. Its cliffs are one height and run as long unbroken level sets. Node shocks start from nothing at a point, grow, hook and merge, and any source works (Worley gives scales). That is the real uniqueness. Below breaking time the node is the same formula as nested DomainOffset, so the skew regime alone would be a graph recipe; only the shock regime is new. Pinhole counts reproduce exactly on seed 1337, but the counter misleads. Against a converged reference (locked K65, cross-checked with unlocked K33 N6, 0.05-0.06% apart at t=1.5) bisection N5 has 3.71% of pixels on the wrong root with 42 thick islands, entropy K13 N4 0.84% with 16. Entropy K13 is not nearly pinhole free: its small region count is worse than bisection in all 4 cases tested, 25/43 vs 12/28, 134/842 vs 33/287, 172/382 vs 73/177, 34/134 vs 10/76 (islands/px), because sliding taps fray the shock edges. Locking taps to a world lattice along d removes the fray at the same K: K13 pol2 gives 2/2 at t=1.5 seed 1337 (6/45 on seed 90210, where the panels look clean but shock ends still count), 18/49 at oct 5. At t=3 K13 looks clean but 6.8% of pixels sit on the wrong side of a moved shock, so K21 pol1 (0.85%, 4/38) is needed if placement matters. Scalar measured: bisect N5 10.2x, lock K9 pol2 15.9x, lock K13 pol2 18.4x, entropy K13 N4 21.1x, lock K21 pol1 24.8x, entropy K21 N4 27.7x perlin2. Eval counts are 5, 11, 15, 17, 22, 25, so the clean root is still 3x bisection in evals; ESTIMATE from measured Perlin 0.93/2.18/4.2 ns AVX2: K13 pol2 about 14/33/63 ns plus bookkeeping, far above the 5x guideline, and it multiplies whatever source is attached. No spectral peak at the tap period (1.73 vs reference 1.92 peak/median). Contraction bound: breaking time at gain .5 lac 2 over 3 seeds is .366-.368 oct 1, .273-.304 oct 3, .230-.240 oct 5, .181-.188 oct 8; it keeps falling with octaves at gain x lac = 1. Gain .35 saturates, .303-.313 oct 5, .300-.319 oct 8. Below the bound bisection N5 is exact to 0.02 with rms .0002-.0007, fixed point is worse at equal evals: N5 .001-.003, N3 .004-.011, N2 .010-.026, and above the bound it makes rings, no fronts. High octave torn shingles at gain .5 are confirmed in every solver and are not a root problem. Gain .35 fixes most of it: K21 pol2 3/19 vs 11/51, K13 pol1 1/10 seed 1337, 17/17 seed 90210, and relief reads as rocky cuestas, at 86.5x perlin2 scalar for 5 octaves. Steepening octave 1 only is 23.5x, but in relief the fronts largely drown under raw detail, so the prototyper's recommended graph is the cheap option, not the better look. Flaws left: hard jumps alias by design; Perlin shows a brick weave in wide views (Simplex does not); hybrid Angle with lock mode shows hatch fringes at angvar 1 and up; hybrid Time needs a Max Time member so tap spacing stays fixed (tested with tvar=3, tmax=1.5, no seams). 3D measured and rendered. 4D and GenTileable2D not tested. No real SIMD node was built.
critic.improved: New mode 7, world locked taps with exact Hopf-Lax on the piecewise linear interpolant and 0 to 2 false position polish steps. Fixes frayed shock edges and holes at the same K, 14 percent cheaper than entropy K13 N4 in scalar at K13 pol1. sheet, thumb and relief overwritten with K13 pol2. Previous source kept as t_burgers_steepen.prev.cpp.

tournament.notes: Keeper, with caveats. Ramps ending in cliffs hold on seeds 1337 and 90210, at window 16 and at far coords. A stock Modulus sawtooth gets one-sided cliffs at a measured 4.59/7.75/12.60 ns AVX2, about a third of my node estimate, but with one cliff height and unbroken level sets. Node shocks start, grow, hook and merge, and any source works, which is why it still ships. Below breaking time it is the same formula as nested DomainOffset, so only the shock regime is new. Suggested Root enum: Fast (bisection, for below breaking time) and Exact (locked taps). Cost is the weak point: K13 pol2 is 15 source evals, ESTIMATE about 14/33/63 ns on Perlin, far over the 5x guideline, multiplied by whatever source is attached. Flaws left: hard jumps alias by design, Perlin shows a brick weave in wide views (Simplex does not), hybrid Angle gives hatch fringes at angvar 1 and up, and hybrid Time needs a Max Time member to keep tap spacing fixed (tested with tvar=3, tmax=1.5, no seams). 3D measured and rendered. 4D and tiling not tested.

master.one_liner: Solves v = Source(p - t*v*d) per sample, so any noise steepens like a breaking wave into sharp one-sided shock fronts, dunes and shingles for about 5 source evals.
master.look: Verified in prototype. Smooth windward ramps ending in razor-sharp leeward cliffs; asymmetric sawtooth skyline. t=0.5 gives skewed noise, t=1.5 gives dunes and fault scarps, t=3 on 2 octaves gives shattered shards with flat tops. Spatially varying Angle gives feather or petal flakes. Good for dunes, wave crests, rock strata, shingled scales, wood-burl faults, wind-sculpted terrain. Feeding it SineWave gives asymmetric ripple marks.
master.algorithm: This is the implicit characteristic solution of inviscid Burgers u_t + (u.d)u_grad = 0. Solve the scalar root of f(v) = Source(p - t*v*d) - v. For |Source|<=B, f(-B)>=0 and f(B)<=0, so a bracket always exists and bisection never diverges. lo=-B, hi=B, flo=B, fhi=-B; repeat N (4..6): v=(lo+hi)/2; f=Source(p - t*v*d) - v; m=f>0; lo=Select(m,v,lo); flo=Select(m,f,flo); hi=Select(m,hi,v); fhi=Select(m,fhi,f). Final false-position step with no extra eval: return lo + (hi-lo)*flo/Max(flo-fhi,1e-6). d is a unit vector from Angle (2D) or a normalised direction member (3D/4D). Prototype: dyn_lens mode=26,N=5,t=1.5,polish=1.
master.why_new: Nothing on the contact sheet is directionally asymmetric. Warps move features but never make slopes one-sided. No graph of existing nodes can do it because the warp amount depends on the node's own output (a true feedback fixed point).
master.simd_plan: Fixed N, all Select, no per-lane exit. Dimension-agnostic GenT over the pack. Cost N x Source: 5 evals, about 5x the source (Perlin 2D about 6 ns, 3D about 11 ns, 4D about 22 ns). A wrapper over a GeneratorSource, so it composes with FBm. 3D form prototyped with perlin3: the XZ slice shows the same shock structure. N=4 with false position already has no visible banding; N=5..7 plain bisection shows stair stripes in hillshade.
master.continuity: C1-ish below breaking time t < 1/max(-dn/ds). Above it, deliberately discontinuous at shock fronts (Select branch in the bisection, measured c0ratio 1.0). Range stays inside the source range.
master.params: Time t (hybrid: 0 returns the source untouched, so a mask can localise steepening), Angle (hybrid in 2D, varying it gives flakes), Iterations int, GeneratorSource Source.
master.risks: Bisection picks a consistent but not entropy-correct root, so shock positions are not physically exact and small pinholes appear at very large t. Source must be roughly within the bracket B. Hybrid angle at high variation can look messy. In GenTileable2D the constant 4D direction projects to a varying direction across the image, though it still tiles because the result is a pure function of 4D position.
master.cost_note: Cost N x Source: 5 evals, about 5x the source (Perlin 2D about 6 ns, 3D about 11 ns, 4D about 22 ns).

plate-drift.look: A field of convex polygonal plates, each visibly rotated and shifted as a rigid body, separated by wedge gaps that open and close; some plate pairs touch, some leave wide triangular voids. Reads as river ice breaking up, cracked dry mud, tempered glass. Rotation sweep 0 / 0.3 / 0.8 rad shows plates turning against their neighbours; drift sweep 0 to 0.5 opens the gaps and scatters the plates. master.one_liner: Voronoi plates that each shrink, slide and rotate as rigid polygons (via the per-cell polygonal gauge evaluated in the plate's own frame), producing ice floes, shattered glass, drying-mud curls and cobbles with variable sand gaps where the gap width and plate rotation are real, not painted.
master.look: A field of convex polygonal plates each slightly rotated and shifted, with wedge-shaped gaps that open and close, some edges touching, some overlapping (dead leaves), like river ice breaking up, a dropped plate, tempered glass, kintsugi gaps, or curling mud. With Drift as a hybrid noise, gaps open in bands (rift zones) and close elsewhere. The sheet has no cells with real variable gaps or rotated plate outlines.
master.algorithm:
Params: Drift (hybrid, cell units <= 0.3), Rotation (hybrid, radians), Gap (hybrid, 0..1 shrink), Bevel, Priority enum {Random, Nearest}, Mode {Margin, Lookup, PlateValue, TiltedHeight}, Source, Jitter.

Window 3^d around the sample. For every cell j precompute site c_j (jittered), rigid transform: translation t_j = Drift*rnd01*rndDir(h_j), rotation R_j (2D: angle = Rotation*rnd11(h_j), one sin/cos per candidate or a cheap normalised (1, eps*rnd11) direction; 3D: rotation about a hashed axis by a small angle, or z-only), shrink s_j = 1 - Gap*(0.5 + 0.5 rnd01), priority pr_j = rnd01.
For each candidate plate i: p_i = R_i^T (p - c_i - t_i) + c_i (bring the sample into plate i's undeformed frame). Polygonal gauge of plate i at p_i: g_i = max over j != i of 2 (p_i - c_i).(c_j - c_i) / |c_j - c_i|^2 (0 at the site, 1 on every Voronoi wall of cell i; this is rel_gauge's PolyGauge). Inside_i = g_i < s_i; signed margin m_i = s_i - g_i.
Outputs: Margin = max_i m_i (positive inside a plate, negative in gaps; clamp(m/Bevel) gives bevelled plates with gaps). Winner w = argmax over inside_i of pr_i (dead leaves where drifted plates overlap) or of m_i (Nearest, no visible overlap). Lookup = Source.Gen(seed ^ h_w, p_w - c_w [, z]) so the texture rides with the plate; PlateValue = rnd11(h_w); TiltedHeight = per-plate plane in plate coordinates. Gap value = constant or distance via Margin.
Why the gauge is enough: the walls that decide whether plate i covers p are the ones between c_i and p, formed by sites near that segment, all inside the 3^d window around p; sites at the window edge only have inaccurate far walls which cannot reach p under the Drift/Jitter bounds (proto audits against brute force like dcc_edgecheck did for edge distance).
master.why_new: CellPatchDomain rotates the texture inside a cell but the cell outline stays put; F2-F1 cannot open wedge gaps or rotate outlines; stamps/dead leaves cannot make the shards fit each other. Displacing the actual polygon pointwise needs the gauge-in-plate-frame trick.
master.simd_plan: Standard 3^d window, nested loop candidates x neighbours of dot products only (no sqrt in the inner loop): 2D 9x8=72 FMA-dots plus 9 cheap rotations, roughly 10-14 ns (3x CellularDistance 2D). 3D Full: 27x26 dots (~60-90 ns) with sites recomputed from hashes inside the inner loop to avoid spilling 81 registers; default 3D/4D is Extruded (plates in xy, z/w passed to the Source), which keeps GenTileable2D usable via an explicit Period rather than the 4D torus.
master.continuity: Margin mode is C0: each m_i is continuous in p, and a candidate entering or leaving the window at a cell boundary has margin far below the max under the Drift bound. Lookup, PlateValue and TiltedHeight are discontinuous at plate edges by design.
master.params: Drift (hybrid), Rotation (hybrid), Gap (hybrid), Bevel, Priority enum, Mode enum, Source, Jitter, 3D mode enum {Extruded, Full}.
master.risks: Needs the brute-force audit of window reach versus Drift/Jitter; expensive in true 3D; dead-leaves overlaps can expose the far (inaccurate) walls of window-edge plates if Drift is pushed past the bound, so clamp Drift in the setter.

master.one_liner: An exact viscous Burgers solution along a wind direction, evaluated pointwise from K taps, giving long windward ramps and crisp slip faces.
master.look: Transverse dune fields: wavy crest lines roughly across the wind, smooth backs and sharp one-sided drops, with barchan-like horns where crests break up. With fBm sources it reads as wind-carved rock or sastrugi. nu slides from soft swell to knife-edged slip face. Clearly asymmetric, unlike anything on the contact sheet.
master.algorithm: Treat source S as potential Phi. Wind unit vector d, time t, viscosity nu, reach R. Taps s_k = R(2k/(K-1)-1), E_k = S(p - s_k d) + s_k^2/(2t), Emin = min E_k. Integrate exp(-E/nu) exactly over the piecewise-linear E between neighbouring taps, which removes banding: a=(E_k-Emin)/nu, b=(E_{k+1}-Emin)/nu, D=b-a, I0=(e^-a - e^-b)/D, I1=(e^-a - e^-b*(1+D))/D^2, with a Taylor fallback I0=e^-a, I1=e^-a/2 selected by mask for small |D|. W += I0, U += s_k*I0 + (s_{k+1}-s_k)*I1. Output u = U/(W*R)*gain. This is the Cole-Hopf solution of u_t + u u_x = nu u_xx: u is the Boltzmann mean displacement along the wind.
master.why_new: Nothing in FastNoise makes a consistently one-sided profile. Ridged, PingPong and Abs are all symmetric, and warps smear rather than form shocks. The shock position, merging and crest spacing come from real conservation-law behaviour, and the node works on any input graph. The exact segment integral was the key finding: K=7 with exact segments looked cleaner than K=13 with plain taps.
master.simd_plan: A 1D search, so K is the same in every dimension. K=7-9 taps plus K FS::Exp calls and one masked Select per segment. On Perlin at K=7 roughly 13/20/35 ns for 2D/3D/4D (scalar prototype 8.5x perlin2). No lattice. Dimension agnostic because only the wind vector changes.
master.continuity: C1 for nu>0 with a smooth source: the output is a ratio of smooth positive integrals, so shocks are steep ramps and not jumps. Measured c0ratio 7.92 with max slope about 30 per unit at nu=0.03. Becoming discontinuous only as nu goes to 0.
master.params: Wind X/Y/Z/W (hybrid for bending wind per lane), Time t (hybrid; dunes sharpen and migrate), Viscosity nu (hybrid), Reach R (float), K (int). Hybrids are read once at p. R should cover t*max|grad S|, or shocks are clipped.
master.risks: Tileable 4D has no uniform wind plane, so the wind direction varies around the torus and the look needs checking. High octave sources need K=13 or more, because tap spacing must resolve the source. Exp in FS has its own cost and range, and subtracting Emin keeps values safe.
master.cost_note: On Perlin at K=7 roughly 13/20/35 ns for 2D/3D/4D (scalar prototype 8.5x perlin2).

fractal-shear-cascade.look: Self mode: a swirly, sheared FBm; relief is ordinary rugged FBm mountains with a slight swirl, in kind the same as DomainWarpGradient or a curl warp feeding FBm. With a strata source the octave zero loops do not read as faults at any setting tried: at slip 0.2 and 1 to 3 octaves the layers become serrated wavy bands with small squiggles, fault width 0.01 to 0.3 and cumulative versus non-cumulative offsets make no visible difference, and slip 0.5 to 2 on a single octave shreds the strata into chaotic curls. No straight traces, no clean offsets, no cross-cutting. The tangential sign-flipping displacement across a closed loop reads as rotation of the inside against the outside, i.e. an eddy, not a strike-slip fault. Second pass: the ridged variant (open faults at |v| = 0.3 instead of closed zero loops) was rendered at gentle settings, 2 octaves, slip 0.1 and 0.2, width 0.05, on strata: the layer edges become jagged saw-tooth bands, indistinguishable in kind from the closed-loop rows above them; still no straight traces and no clean offsets. The idea's own proposed fix does not change the verdict.

critic.notes: Closed-loop shear faults do not read as tectonic. Confirmed on seed 90210 and window 24: octave 1 slip .15 width .02 gives saw-tooth layer edges, width and cumulative make no real difference, larger slip shreds into camouflage and stained glass, ridged mode has the same jagged edges. No straight trace, no clean offset, no cross-cutting anywhere. The stated reason is half the story. The tangential sign flip explains the serration, but fixing it would not rescue the idea: a stock rigid Y offset across closed Perlin level sets gives clean offsets with no rotation, and it still reads as lens-shaped blobs. Closed curved traces fail on their own; straightness is what sells a fault. I also disagree that self mode is in kind the same as a warp: DomainWarpGradient, Progressive and Independent have no such hairline creases, c0ratio 2.32. That smoke is pretty but untectonic, and shear-flow already covers combed smoke and marble. Scalar measured 8.65x perlin2. Range and far coords fine.

Ridged mode is the same. No fault reading anywhere. Self mode has hairline creases that stock warps lack (c0ratio 2.32), so it is not quite the same as a warp, but it is smoke, not geology, and shear-flow already covers combed smoke and marble. A clean rigid offset across closed loops still reads as lenses, so fixing the tangential flip would not rescue it. Scalar measured 8.65x perlin2. Range and far coords fine.

master.one_liner: Each octave's zero isoline acts as a strike-slip fault: everything finer is displaced along the isoline tangent in opposite directions on the two sides, giving nested fault networks that offset layers and detail at every scale.
master.look: Faulted terrain/texture: coherent slip lines where the pattern is sheared, with bigger faults offsetting smaller ones (coarse to fine order, like old faults cutting young layers). With a striped Source (SineWave) you get textbook displaced strata; with FBm you get torn, en-echelon ridge offsets. Clearly different from any warp on the sheet: displacement is tangential and sign-flipping, so it preserves local structure and only breaks continuity visually along the lines.
master.algorithm:
F=0; off=0; amp=1; freq=1
  for i in 0..Octaves-1:
    (v, dv) = gradSimplex((p+off)*freq, seed+i)
    F += amp*v
    t = perp(dv) * InvSqrt(dot(dv,dv)+eps)      // 2D isoline tangent, unit; 3D: t = normalize(dv x e_i) with e_i a per-octave hashed constant direction; 4D: t = normalize(dv x e_i x f_i) or drop to 2 planar perps
    sgn = Min(Max(v / FaultWidth, -1), 1)         // soft sign, C0 (optionally smoothstep for C1)
    off += Slip * amp * sgn * t / freq            // slip proportional to fault size
    amp*=Gain; freq*=Lacunarity
  // optional final 'Strata' stage: out = Source((p+off)*freq_final) with the user's own Source (stripes, cellular, ...) so the faults offset a chosen pattern; mode 'Self' returns F.
  out = F / sum(amp)  (or Source value)
master.why_new: Sign-flipping tangential displacement across an octave's own isoline cannot be built from existing warps (no gradients, no per-octave sign gating). Geologists' 'strike-slip' look at multiple scales is missing in every noise library I know.
master.simd_plan: Branch-free, reuses gradient kernel. Window: none beyond kernels. Cost ~1.7x Simplex per octave 2D, ~2x in 3D (cross product + normalise). 5 octaves ~10 ns/sample 2D AVX2 estimate. Per-octave e_i directions precomputed when seed/params set (small table).
master.continuity: C0 with the clamp soft-sign (jump in derivative across the fault zone of width FaultWidth); C1 if FaultWidth>0 and smoothstep is used. Never discontinuous in value; a FaultWidth near 0 looks discontinuous but samples still vary continuously, so no NaN or seam problems.
master.params: Octaves int, Gain hybrid, Lacunarity, Slip hybrid (slip distance in units of the octave's feature size), FaultWidth hybrid, Mode enum {Self, Source}, Source (GeneratorSource for Source mode), Seed Offset.
master.risks: Fault lines are the zero sets of each octave, so they are closed loops at coarse scale, not infinite fault traces; a Ridged-style |v| variant turns them into open ridge faults. 4D form needs a decision on the slip direction.
master.cost_note: Cost ~1.7x Simplex per octave 2D, ~2x in 3D (cross product + normalise). 5 octaves ~10 ns/sample 2D AVX2 estimate.

proto_index.params_text: oct=4,slip=0.35,width=0.08,smooth=1,out=0 (self, smoky hairlines); out=1,oct=1,slip=0.15,width=0.02 (gentlest strata test, still no offset)
